exit_state: The bank path separates deposits, settlement cash, credit allowance and regulatory measures. Its scoped prudential reconciliation constructs the allowance-cap base before excess deductions and leaves missing leverage averages unresolved. The richer loss formula retains exposure/severity dependence. Asset classification now distinguishes amortised cost, debt/equity FVOCI and FVTPL; a modified-time-value example begins the contractual cash-flow test and continues next.
findings: The Apple Card commitment's legal date, later announcement and expected closing remain separate; future estimated loans are not treated as already owned.
The prudential case defines a distinct book and historical rule scope, including common-stock eligibility, ordinary corporate exposure and central-bank cash assumptions.
The allowance-cap formula uses the pre-excess base; the text demonstrates why solving a circular alternative accurately would still compute the wrong regulatory quantity.
A failed deposit payment leaves the liability and default visible despite unchanged capital ratios. Debt/equity FVOCI also retain different recycling rules. No new confirmed local defect.
